notes.note: Rows #0.4-0.11 (with 0.4-0.6 in story_033) are party-leader variants of the same 'this cannon could arm the Ride Machine' line; #0.7 is the brasher 'just right' variant. No speaker recovered.
Source sets Gaia Cannon in brackets; kept in quotes. Team Trinity written without quotes, matching earlier slices. #0.18/#0.34 repeat the second sentence as a split variant.
Source ends with '!?'; kept as a taunting 'got it!?'.
#0.20-0.27: eight party-leader variants of the same line (story_035's 0246 copy lists Wing Zero, Nu, Zeta, OOO, W, Den-O, Zero, Mebius). Only the first carries a recovered speaker (Mebius).
No speaker recovered; #0.36/#0.39 are tagged Mebius, but the line ('you are no Gundams') reads like 00 (Setsuna). Kept speaker-neutral.
Johann asking whether they mean to fight fellow Gundams; restored subject 'You mean to'.
Ali al-Saachez's catchphrase 'tokoro ga gicchon' rendered 'Not so fast!!' (common fan rendering; no glossary entry).
'Gaki' = the Trinity siblings; the client (Regis higher-ups) has no more use for them.
'Icchimai na' read as 'itte shimai na' (go and die/drop dead) as he kills Michael.
No speaker recovered; rough tone suggests Den-O Sword Form (Momotaros), the leader tagged at #0.76.
No speaker recovered; Arche Gundam greeting the heroes, before repeating #0.69-70 as #0.86-87.
Tagged Arche Gundam but likely the party's silent reaction after he leaves; kept as '......'.
No speaker recovered; Sandrock arriving (next row Sandrock: 'Are you all right?').

#0.91-0.104 are party-leader reply pairs to Sandrock (the #0.91 Sandrock tag is an extractor carry-over). Register follows the source: #0.97 plainer, #0.99-0.100 polite (likely Mebius/OOO), #0.101/#0.103 'We're fine'. Maganac-tai = Maganac Corps.

report: 80/80 rows. Many party-leader variant rows with no recovered speaker; speaker tags on #0.36-39 (Mebius) and #0.88/#0.91 look like extractor carry-overs. 'Tokoro ga gicchon' -> 'Not so fast!!' (Ali catchphrase, not in glossary). 'Maganac Corps' used for Maganac-tai (glossary note only).
